target.name: Rain Industries

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Rain Industries is a Seed-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $14.7M to date. The broader sector includes 7 private peers (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, Elroy Air among them) and no public comparables, limiting the depth of available valuation anchors.

Given the early stage and capital raised to date, a Stage-Progression methodology is applicable. Using $15M (total raised) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $37M. A Peer-Median approach could not be applied; while five same-sector peers exist, none provided sufficient data points at the same or adjacent stages with comparable valuation tiers to establish a reliable median. Relying on all-sector median without stage-specificity would introduce unacceptable bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $31M to $42M, with a median estimate of $37M. This range reflects the Stage-Progression result with applied variance bands. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-peer stage data—which would strengthen conviction around capital-efficiency benchmarks—and limited visibility into Rain Industries' revenue traction, capital efficiency, or competitive positioning relative to the identified peer set. The single-method foundation warrants treating this as directional rather than definitive.
